text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The Bulgarian lev collapsed to an all-time low of 360 to the dollar in the cash forex market, marking the start of hyperinflation, dealers said.
-- Pupils and teachers from a technical high school blocked a main road in the capital Sofia to protest against the lack of heating in their school.
-- Domestic electricity prices are expected to rise by 14 percent from December 1, the energy ministry said.
-- The majority of leaders of parties within the main opposition Union of Democratic Forces said they opposed transforming the coalition into a party.
-- Bulgaria's domestic debt rose by 27.7 billion levs in October to 668.3 billion levs due to new issues of government securities and the fall of the lev, the finance ministry said.

-- Bulgaria's parliament will revise the 1996 state budget for the second time this year, as the budget deficit in November is expected to be 10 percent over the annual target, finance minister Dimitar Kostov said.

-- Bulgaria's industrial exports in the first half of 1996 fell by $1 billion over the same period last year due to the economic crisis and lack of operating capital of industrial firms, industry minister Lyubomir Dachev said.
-- The lev is expected to fall to about 600 to the dollar by the end of the year, experts said.
-- Sofia city transport workers will go on strike if the cabinet fails to meet their demands for a 65 percent pay rise, trade unions said.
-- Chief Prosecutor Ivan Tatarchev said investigations have been launched against officials of 13 commercial banks placed under receivership by the central bank, but declined to specify names.
